newsitem.title: QATAR: TENNIS-MUSTER STRUGGLES INTO QATAR QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER STRUGGLES INTO QATAR QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Top seed Thomas Muster, angered by mobile phone users, dropped a set and took more than two hours to beat Norway's Christian Ruud for a place in the quarter-finals of the $635,000 Qatar Open on Thursday.
The Austrian needed two hours and 13 minutes to defeat Ruud 6-2 3-6 7-5 and set up a last eight clash against American Jim Courier, the eighth seed.

Muster cruised through the first set in just 32 minutes but his game went to pieces in the second when he became increasingly disgruntled by line calls and the constant ringing of mobile telephones inside the stadium court.
At one stage, the Austrian screamed at a spectator: "Turn off your phone or get the hell out of here!"
Ruud, ranked 59th in the world, took full advantage of his opponent's lapse in concentration as he broke the Austrian's service in the eighth game and then held his own serve to win the set 6-3.
The deciding set went with the serve until the Norwegian's nerve failed him in the 12th game and Muster raised his arms in the air in delight and relief at victory.
Muster said afterwards the phones in the crowd had disturbed him.
"If you want to make a telephone call, you should go outside the court. If you want to watch tennis, then watch tennis," he said.

"Things have become much more liberal at tennis matches now, with the crowd being allowed to move around. That's okay, but what's next? Are we going to have people bringing in huge stereo cassette players on their shoulders and having a party in the stands?"

Courier made the last eight with a 6-3 6-4 win over Romanian qualifier Razvan Sabau. Czech defending champion Petr Korda saw off Magnus Norman of Sweden 6-7 (3-7) 6-4 6-2 while Sergi Bruguera defeated fellow Spaniard Javier Sanchez 6-0 6-1.

In Friday's quarter-finals, Muster takes on Courier, Bruguera meets Korda, Sweden's number five seed Magnus Gustafsson faces Britain's Tim Henman and Morocco's Hicham Arazi plays Sweden's Magnus Larsson.
